title: Museum - Work Package 5 - Electricity
description:
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months:

Context:
The CNES wishes to renovate the Space Museum in Kourou, French Guiana, to make it a space adapted to the expectations of its target public. This renovation encompasses all the interior spaces (permanent exhibition, reception area, shop), as well as the building’s cladding and the addition of exterior facilities.
Reflection on the renovation of the Space Museum is part of the strategy to promote in French Guiana the image of space and of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG), Europe’s Spaceport.
The design of the project is global and focuses on attractiveness in order to enhance the visit experience for all visitors: families, school groups, customers, institutions, employees, service providers, and others.
In addition, the project is part of a broader context, in particular associated with:
-	The modernisation of the image of the Guiana Space Centre (CSG),
-	The improvement of a global tourism offer of the CSG and the expectations regarding the welcoming of visitors,
-	A strong demand for information about the CSG and space activity in French Guiana.

Purpose of the contract:
This information concerns the contracts for works related to museum displays, scenography and graphic aspects.
The work for the CNES/CSG, at the site of the Space Museum at the Guiana Space Centre in Kourou (French Guiana), falls within a demanding operational context (project integrating an architectural and a scenographic component, CSG environment, location), which the contractor will need to take into account in their bid.
Please note that the renovation project is also the subject of a BIM-GEM (Building Information Modelling - Management-Operation-Maintenance) strategy from the design stage through to the use of the structure.
The CNES hereby informs you that the activities detailed below will be subject to a European tender procedure with publication on ESA-STAR in the coming months. These activities are part of the renovation of the Space Museum.

Work to be carried out will include:

?	Removal of some existing installations
?	Removal of the thematic equipment from the mezzanines, all transformers from the staircase strip lights and the guard rails
?	Reworking of evacuation plans and instructions,
?	Modification of the main electrical cabinet (TDP),
?	Reworking of TNC power supplies from existing distribution panels,
? (Optional) Commissioning of a 40 kVA electrical UPS adapted to the needs of the "high backup current" installation
? (Optional) Implementation of the High Quality Power General and Distribution panel,
?	Implementation of normal and backup electrical lighting,
? Implementation of electrical power needed to supply scenographic lighting,
? Implementation of a presence detector to manage lighting equipment,
?	Implementation of a server lighting management system,
? Implementation of a power installation, power point, power supply and air conditioning,
?	Review of FO and Telecom inputs on the Multimedia Bay and computer engineering and network
?	Reworking of the type 1 fire alarm system 
? Implementation of a network of equipotential, local and additional bonding
? The establishment of a network of high current/low current cable trays, tubing, plastic ducts and ducts necessary for the routing of pipes
? Implementation of an internal telephone installation and a computer pre-wiring installation in category 6
?	(Optional) Implementation of a WIFI installation
?	(Optional) Reworking of the burglar alarm system installation
?	Implementation of a system for controlling access to the Museum space
?	Implementation of a videotelephony installation for the secure waiting area

title: Gymnasium im Schloss - Neubau Entlastungsbau II - Spezialtiefbau
description: Inhalt der Ausschreibung Planung und Ausführung von ca. 75 Bohrpfählen in Längen von 12-16m und Durchmessern von 50-60cm. Abspitzen dieser Pfähle auf Niveau Unterkante Stahlbeton-Tragrost; Ausführung Tragrost bauseits. Gffls. Vorbohren durch eventuell vorhandene Steinschichten aus historischer Befestigungsanlage. Allgemein Die Stadt Wolfenbüttel beabsichtigt auf dem Gelände des Gymnasiums im Schloss die Baumaßnahme „GIS Erweiterungsbau II“ umzusetzen: - Den Abbruch des bestehenden Biologie-Bestandsgebäudes - Sicherung und teilweise Instandsetzung der Fundament-Mauerreste - Sicherung der Kasematte - Den Neubau eines zweiten Erweiterungsbaus mit allgemeinen Unterrichtsräumen und den Fachunterrichtsräumen für Kunst/ Werken, Darstellendes Spiel und Biologie Lage Das Gymnasium im Schloss liegt im historischen Zentrum der Stadt Wolfenbüttel, angrenzend an den Seeliger Park, die Seeliger Villa und in direkter Nachbarschaft zur Landesmusikakademie. Der geplante Anbau schließt orthogonal als Riegel an den 2013 fertiggestellten Entlastungsbau I (Spiegelschloss) in Analogie zu den bestehenden Geschosshöhen an und tritt an die Stelle des 1- geschossigen, abgängigen Bestandsgebäudes der Biologie. Das Baufeld befindet sich auf dem Grundstück des Schlosses Wolfenbüttel/ Schule GIS das an die Innenstadt Wolfenbüttels, den „Okerumflutgraben“ mit den alten Festungsanlagen und den „Seeliger Park“ angrenzt. Entwurf Der Entwurf zeigt einen kompakten, 3-geschossigen Schul-Erweiterungsanbau, der orthogonal zum GIS I gesetzt ist und über eine Fuge in Form eines Atriums vom Bestand abgelöst wird. Die Zugänge in das Gebäude befinden sich im Norden am Atrium und im Westen in der Achse zur Kasematte. Innerhalb des Erweiterungsbaus werden die verschiedenen Ebenen durch ein Treppenhaus im Osten, in direkter Flucht der angrenzenden Kasematte und im Norden über das Treppenhaus im angrenzenden Bestandsbau GiS I erschlossen. Konstruktion Der Neubau ist als Stahlbeton-Skelettbau mit Holzhybrid-Decken und massivem (STB) WC- und Technikkern geplant. Die Außenwände bestehen aus einer nichttragenden Holztafelbauweise mit vorgehängter Ziegel-Fassade. Aufgrund des schwierigen Baugrunds und der archäologischen Befunde wird eine Pfahlgründung mit Pfahlkopfbalken und darüber spannender Bodenplatte umgesetzt. Im Bereich der Ausgrabungen wird die Bodenplatte ausgespart und dem Innen- und Außenraum erlebbar gemacht.

title: 10044493 - Climate resilient urban development and financing in selected municipalities in Zambia
description: Objective of the assignment: The project "Just and Climate Resilient Urban Development and Decentralisation in Zambia" (CitiZen+D), implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ), supports urban development and decentralisation in Zambia in four output areas: Output 1: The coordination, planning, and implementation capacities of selected cities for equitable and climate-resilient urban development have been improved. Output 2: The financial capacities of selected cities for equitable and climate-resilient urban development have improved. Output 3: The participation of civil society actors, especially women, in the implementation of equitable and climate-resilient urban development has improved. Output 4: The professional exchange between government and civil society actors on successful approaches to equitable, climate-resilient urban development has improved. Under Output 1, the programme supports the development of 1 Planning Agreement and 5 Local Area Plans (LAPs) in the cities of Choma, Mazabuka, and Livingstone in Southern Province and Mansa and Samfya in Luapula. In 2025 the programme was focusing on the selection of informal settlements in the respective cities and on developing a planning and implementation framework for the development of the LAPs. Based on this the LAP process was initiated in Mansa and Livingstone. To progress with the remaining cities CitiZen+D is looking for a contractor supporting the preparation of three LAPs and one Planning Agreement in Choma (LAP), Samfya (LAP), and Mazabuka (LAP). The location of the Planning Agreement is yet to be determined. The local area plans are meant to: - Guide sustainable land use and development, for example safeguard natural sensitive areas, such as for water catchment and wildlife - Improve infrastructure and service delivery - Support climate change adaptation - Align with national and regional planning strategies The contractor will assist local authorities in designing a participatory planning approach that integrates climate resilience while including the views and opinions of residents, including women, elderly, youth and other marginalized groups. To achieve active inclusion and consideration of communities and marginalized groups, the contractor will sub-contract civil society organizations for the LAP in Choma and Mazabuka through a financing instrument (local subsidy). In order to strengthen planning capacities and use of Geographic Information Systems the contractor is expected to implement and coordinate a local subsidy with the University of Zambia (UNZA). Once the Local Area Plans are approved the contractor shall support local authorities in developing a comprehensive and context-sensitive implementation concept for the LAPs targeting the selected settlements. This concept will outline actionable strategies, institutional frameworks, and phased interventions to formalize land tenure, improve access to basic services (water, sanitation, waste management, and mobility), and enhance housing conditions while preserving community livelihoods. The concept needs to explicitly emphasis on identifying, structuring, and accessing viable financing options to ensure real-world execution. The output will empower local authorities and partners to move beyond planning into funded, scalable, and accountable implementation that delivers tangible improvements in housing, infrastructure, and livelihoods for informal settlement residents. This includes strengthening of resource mobilisation in local authorities. The assignment is structured in the following work packages to be implemented by the contractor: Work Package Title Work Package 1 Climate resilient local area planning and planning agreements Work Package 2 CSO support for inclusive Local Area Plans (LAPs) Work Package 3 GIS capacities for local authorities Work Package 4 Financing models for LAP implementation Work Package 5 Strengthening national dialogue Work Package 6 Strengthening resource mobilisation Work Package 7 Support processes (Expert Pool)
